### The Single Highest-Leverage Change: Add the Five Missing Slides

Your deck currently has 6 slides. The seed-stage standard (per Sequoia, DocSend, and YC frameworks) is 10–12 slides. You are not missing minor supporting slides — you are missing the five slides that investors most want to see before writing a check:

1. **Why Now** — "Why wasn't this built three years ago?" is one of the first questions a VC asks internally. Sequoia's framework requires an explicit catalyst: a market shift, a new infrastructure layer, a change in developer behavior. Without it, your deck reads as a solution in search of a moment.

2. **Market Sizing** — There is no TAM/SAM/SOM, no bottom-up calculation, no market size figure anywhere. Per Sequoia, bottom-up sizing (number of indie SaaS founders x willingness to pay x realistic adoption rate) is non-negotiable. Investors cannot size the opportunity. They will not proceed.

3. **Competition** — No competitive landscape means investors fill in the blank themselves, usually pessimistically. DocSend research shows VCs spend 88% more time on the competition slide in funded decks versus unfunded ones. The absence of this slide is not neutral — it actively signals either naivety or evasion. Name the alternatives: individual tool CLIs, Zapier, Raycast, manual integration. Then show why your wedge is different.

4. **Business Model** — The only financial signal in your deck is "$8K MRR, 24 customers," which implies ~$333/customer/month. But investors don't know: Is this a per-seat model? Usage-based? What's your gross margin? Who is the buyer vs. the user? Per Sequoia's framework, these are required at seed stage.

5. **GTM** — You have 24 paying customers but no explanation of how you got them. What's the acquisition channel? What's the CAC? Is this founder-led sales or product-led growth? Per Sequoia/DocSend, ICP + channel + early proof (pipeline, conversion, CAC) are required. The traction number means more when you can explain how it's reproducible.

Adding these five slides moves your deck from an incomplete signal to a fundable narrative. Storydoc benchmark data shows decks with fewer than 7 slides have a fail threshold for completion rates — you are at exactly 6.

Every slide headline is currently a topic label: "PROBLEM", "SOLUTION", "TRACTION", "TEAM", "ASK". Per DocSend and Sequoia's core principle, investors skim headlines first in the ~2:30 they spend on a shared deck. Each headline should be a conclusion they can act on.

Per Sequoia/DocSend, the solution slide should show the workflow transformation: what does a founder's day look like before Acmecorp, and what does it look like after? ## Coaching Commentary

### What's Working — Protect These

**You have real traction, and it shows.** $8K MRR, 24 paying customers, and 18% MoM growth in four months is a credible signal at seed stage. This is the most investor-attention-grabbing fact in your deck, and it appears on Slide 4 — which is exactly where DocSend data says it needs to land. If investors reach Slide 4, 82% finish the deck. Your traction slide is doing its job.

**The problem is quantified.** "20+ hours/week on developer tooling integration" gives investors a concrete anchor. Most pre-seed founders write vague problem statements ("founders waste time"). You've named a specific, measurable pain. That specificity builds credibility.

**The founding team has a pedigree that fits the product.** Ex-Stripe (engineering) and ex-Notion (product) is a strong signal for a developer-tooling company. Investors will respect why these two people are building this — the instinct is right, even if the slide execution needs work (more on that below).

### The Single Highest-Leverage Change: Add the Five Missing Slides

Your deck currently has 6 slides. The seed-stage standard (per Sequoia, DocSend, and YC frameworks) is 10–12 slides. You are not missing minor supporting slides — you are missing the five slides that investors most want to see before writing a check:

1. **Why Now** — "Why wasn't this built three years ago?" is one of the first questions a VC asks internally. Sequoia's framework requires an explicit catalyst: a market shift, a new infrastructure layer, a change in developer behavior. Without it, your deck reads as a solution in search of a moment.

2. **Market Sizing** — There is no TAM/SAM/SOM, no bottom-up calculation, no market size figure anywhere. Per Sequoia, bottom-up sizing (number of indie SaaS founders x willingness to pay x realistic adoption rate) is non-negotiable. Investors cannot size the opportunity. They will not proceed.

3. **Competition** — No competitive landscape means investors fill in the blank themselves, usually pessimistically. DocSend research shows VCs spend 88% more time on the competition slide in funded decks versus unfunded ones. The absence of this slide is not neutral — it actively signals either naivety or evasion. Name the alternatives: individual tool CLIs, Zapier, Raycast, manual integration. Then show why your wedge is different.

4. **Business Model** — The only financial signal in your deck is "$8K MRR, 24 customers," which implies ~$333/customer/month. But investors don't know: Is this a per-seat model? Usage-based? What's your gross margin? Who is the buyer vs. the user? Per Sequoia's framework, these are required at seed stage.

5. **GTM** — You have 24 paying customers but no explanation of how you got them. What's the acquisition channel? What's the CAC? Is this founder-led sales or product-led growth? Per Sequoia/DocSend, ICP + channel + early proof (pipeline, conversion, CAC) are required. The traction number means more when you can explain how it's reproducible.

Adding these five slides moves your deck from an incomplete signal to a fundable narrative. Storydoc benchmark data shows decks with fewer than 7 slides have a fail threshold for completion rates — you are at exactly 6.

Every slide headline is currently a topic label: "PROBLEM", "SOLUTION", "TRACTION", "TEAM", "ASK". Per DocSend and Sequoia's core principle, investors skim headlines first in the ~2:30 they spend on a shared deck. Each headline should be a conclusion they can act on.

Per Sequoia/DocSend, the solution slide should show the workflow transformation: what does a founder's day look like before Acmecorp, and what does it look like after?
